components.title: Adults using each way of reading in 2025 (%), one person may use several

components.text: Digital reading rose from 64.0% to 80.8% of adults in ten years, and has barely moved since 2019.

notes: What changed is how people read. In 2025, 79.0% of adults read on a phone, 66.4% read online on a computer, 38.7% listened to books, 21.3% used an e-reader and 6.3% watched videos about books. These overlap, since one person can read on a phone and listen too, so they do not add up. Listening has grown most steadily: it was 17.0% in 2016. The overall share who read digitally in some way went from 64.0% in 2015 to 79.3% in 2019, then rose only 1.5 points in six years. Its scope also shifted: it still counted CD-ROMs in 2016, and from the 22nd round it explicitly includes listening and book videos.
